Hi Sara —

Quick thanks and yes — we can design a 2-year staged prepay with a true-up and an explicit performance buffer. Proposal (high level):

1) Structure
   - Year 1: Upfront prepay for 9 months of expected run-rate, with a Q4 true-up to reflect launch seasonality.
   - Year 2: Prepay for 12 months based on true-up-adjusted run-rate from end of Y1.

2) Safety margin (performance buffer)
   - We recommend a 30% buffer over committed baseline for the first 90 days post-launch (no throttling). Temporary usage beyond that will be billed at a pre-agreed overage rate or covered by a one-time short-term burst credit (see pricing below).

3) Pricing (illustrative)
   - Blended discount target: 18% year 1 (reflecting early ramp risk), 12% year 2 post-true-up.
   - Optional: move to 20% blended if Hearth agrees to accelerate year 1 prepay from 9->12 months (accelerated cash).

I've attached a worked pricing model for the above as a starting point — pricing_model_hearth_v3.xlsx. Ben and Kimberly, can you confirm whether finance needs an escalator/approval for the 18/12 split?

If acceptable, we can turn this into a clean AMP and get legal/procurement language ready.

Cheers,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

- Buffer: 30% for 90 days is fine, but we require an auto-triggered short-term burst billing at 1.6x list after that window; include a monthly hard cap opt-in to avoid surprise bills.
- Compliance: Procurement will ask for invoice schedule and recognition (we should align with revenue ops).

Action items for approval flow:
1) Sales to confirm final numbers in the attached pricing_model_hearth_v3.xlsx (Grace/Ben).
2) Legal to draft SOW language for true-up cadence and burst credit (Grace).
3) Marcus to route to CFO (Marissa) for final blended discount sign-off if requested >19%.

I can provide conditional approval today for 18/12 provided items 1–2 are done and the contract includes the auto-true-up rules.

-Marcus
